_source: Dave Arnold, Liquid Intelligence, 'Structure of different types of drinks' (pdf 129-130, printed pp. 125-126). Formulas: same book, pdf 127 (printed p. 123). Ranges are Arnold's analysis of classic recipes, not laws. Styles hot, highball, collins, fizz, flip and freeform added 2026-09-25 (Robin: 'let's not limit ourselves to any types of drinks'); each note gives its derivation.

built.label: Built (spirit on a rock)
built.note: Arnold gives ~7.6 g/100 ml sugar and no acid; the sugar band is a +/-1 g tolerance around that single figure.

stirred-spirit.label: Stirred, spirit only (no vermouth, no citrus: an Old-Fashioned or CANADIAN served up)
stirred-spirit.note: Stirred dilution and Arnold's stirred strength and sugar ranges, with no acid range: the stirred acid floor assumes vermouth (Tomás's rule candidate, outlaw-regular-guy 2026-10-01; accepted by Robin 2026-10-06, D2).

shaken-spirit.label: Shaken, spirits only (no citrus; e.g. the Stinger)
shaken-spirit.note: Arnold has no category for this; judged against stirred finished ranges for strength and sugar, acid not required.

carbonated.label: Carbonated / sparkling (built, no ice dilution)
carbonated.note: Arnold's newer recipes sit at 14-16%; his older ones ran above 16%, so ABV up to ~20% is 'edge', not 'out', for spirit-backed sparklers.

bowl.label: Punch bowl over a block of ice
bowl.note: Judged after the declared melt against Arnold's finished shaken ranges (closest style).

hot.label: Hot (toddies, hot punches; hot water or tea declared in the recipe)
hot.note: Derived from the Cocktail Codex's three toddies (Old-Fashioned chapter: Hot Toddy 10.6%, a Cognac toddy 11.0%, Gun Club Toddy 12.7%; 'a toddy is really just an Old-Fashioned that swaps in hot water for cold', 4 oz water to 2 oz spirit baseline). Arnold: hot drinks need less sugar than cold (sweetness perception rises with heat) and acid sparingly; too much alcohol stings the nose (Liquid Intelligence pdf 184, 187). Declare the hot water/tea as an ingredient; no ice melt is modelled.

highball.label: Highball (spirit lengthened with soda, tonic, ginger beer… on ice)
highball.note: Derived from the Cocktail Codex's Whisky Highball (2 oz : 6 oz seltzer = 10%; its 2:5 = 11.4%) and Gin and Tonic (15.7%), capped by Arnold's carbonated 14-16%. Mark the lengthener stage: top. A 3-second stir's melt is not modelled.

collins.label: Collins (short-shaken sour, seltzer, served on ice)
collins.note: Derived from the Cocktail Codex's Tom Collins (14.1%) and Moscow Mule (13.2%). The Codex short-shakes 'about five seconds' to leave room for seltzer; the 25% base dilution is our estimate, not a Codex figure. Mark the seltzer stage: top.

fizz.label: Fizz (shaken sour, often with egg white, topped with seltzer, no ice)
fizz.note: Derived from the Cocktail Codex's Silver Fizz (10.9%) and Ramos Gin Fizz (9.0%) ('fizzes are basically Collins-style drinks served without ice'). The base is diluted by Arnold's shaken formula; seltzer (stage: top) is added after. Only two data points, so edges are common: justify them.

blended.label: Blended (frozen, blender with ice)
blended.note: Arnold, Liquid Intelligence pdf 130: initial ranges and ~90% dilution. His finished figures are on an unreadable chart page (pdf 131), so the finished bands are derived (initial / 1.9) and widened slightly.

flip.label: Flip (whole egg or yolk, shaken; hot or cold)
flip.note: Arnold has no flip category; strength and sugar are judged against his egg-white ranges (the closest structure). A Flip or nog has no citrus, so no acid range applies (Robin 2026-10-06, collection review D2). Cocktail Codex root: the Flip. A hot flip belongs under 'hot'.

freeform.label: Freeform (anything no style fits: milk punch, jelly, frozen, spritz…)
freeform.note: Nothing is out of bounds (Robin 2026-09-25). No ranges are applied: the tool reports the numbers and the nearest styles, and the Mixologist justifies the balance in Checks. Declare any added water, melt or top-up in the recipe.

_edge_rule: A value outside its range but within 25% of the range's width (or inside a style's explicit edge_bands) is 'edge': allowed, but the dossier must justify it.

_codex_families._note: The Codex's six root cocktails (Old-Fashioned, Martini, Daiquiri, Sidecar, Whisky Highball, Flip) all have at least one style. No drink type is excluded: anything else is 'freeform'.
